LinSCP command console. Commands run in the live session of this tab (try 'pwd', 'ls', 'stat keep.txt', 'synchronize local -preview', 'session').
lscp>
Workspaces
A workspace reopens the current tabs, their two pane directories and the active tab. Passwords are not stored in it.
Bookmarks
A bookmark stores a directory of one panel or both panels together. It stores no session, password or host key.
Session URL
The URL opens this site in this client. A URL with a password is a secret, never written to the logs.
Import sessions
Sites are read from an OpenSSH client configuration or a FileZilla sitemanager.xml file. Passwords are encrypted with sessions.key when they are stored.
Preferences
These are the defaults a transfer and a confirmation start from. A transfer dialog still lets you change them for one run.
KiB
Customizable installer scripts
Inspect, edit and save the default server installer scripts used for Mosh and remote desktop setup.
Cleanup stored data
Each item is one file or directory this client writes. Removing it cannot be undone, and the parts you leave unticked are not touched.
🖥️ Remote desktop
Open a desktop session on the remote host. RDP (3389, xrdp), VNC (5900, TigerVNC) and SPICE (spice-vdagent) ride the SSH tunnel when a jump is configured. X11 uses SSH. The built-in X2Go KDrive viewer is experimental and requires the KDrive server backend; NX support has been removed.
Wayland sessions use waypipe; X11 uses ssh -X.
Installer script — review before installing
Runs on the server through SSH with sudo when needed. Review the script before running it; available packages and supported distributions vary by service.

WebDAV locks and properties
Key/Session Export
Choose which saved sessions to export. Passwords, key passwords, jump-host credentials and referenced SSH keys are included, so the sessions can be restored on another device with Key/Session Import.
Sessions to export:
The backup password is not saved. The export is a timestamped LinSCP backup; import it with Key/Session Import. All saved session settings, directories, SSH keys, TLS certificates, remembered host keys and transfer presets are included.
Key/Session Import
Choose a key/session backup and read it. Encrypted LinSCP backups and plain-text backups are detected automatically. Tick the sessions you want, then import them. Names already saved are skipped unless you tick Replace saved sessions with the same name below.
Sessions to import:
Full application backup
Export an encrypted backup of saved sessions, all vault SSH keys, workspaces, host keys, bookmarks and preferences. Unlock the vault first. Use a separate password of at least 12 bytes.
Restore replaces saved sessions, vault SSH keys and application settings on this device. Disconnect remote sessions and finish queued transfers first.
Copy or move to another server
WebDAV moves rely on server ETag enforcement. SFTP copies can see concurrent changes; directory copies and cross-server moves are not transactional and may leave partial files.
Files from your file manager
These files were selected in your file manager. Upload them to this tab's remote directory?
Site Manager
Stored sessions
Both panes are directories on this machine; no server is contacted.
Connection resilience (Alt host & auto-reconnect)
The alternate uses Alt Port and the same credentials. Its SSH host key or TLS certificate is checked independently. Automatic fallback applies only to direct SSH or FTP connection failures, not authentication or security errors.
When enabled on a saved session, retry a lost connection and restore it after restart if it was previously open. Save the session to apply changes.
SSH tunnel
SFTP and SCP only. The tunnel and destination host keys are verified separately.
Mosh — Mobile Shell
Starts mosh-server over SSH and switches remote terminals to encrypted UDP for roaming and intermittent networks. File transfers continue over SFTP or SCP. Requires direct UDP reachability (not compatible with SSH jump tunnels or TCP proxies).
Proxy
HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5h ride the proxy; Telnet/CMD runs a local command with %host/%port.
Kerberos (GSSAPI)
Advanced (FTPS/TLS, passive, certificates)
FTPS/TLS settings are stored per-site and honoured by both console and GUI.
Amazon S3 options
Applied to Amazon S3 uploads and object copies on this site.
Remote desktop options
Applied when launching native desktop viewers or generating .rdp/.vv connection tickets.
Choose a private key from the vault

Keys used by stored sessions cannot be deleted. Deleting a vault key does not delete the original file or backups.

SSH host keys
Trusted SSH server host keys remembered in the local vault. Remove a server entry if its key was legitimately rotated, or pre-pin a known server fingerprint.
Server monitor

Read-only Linux telemetry over your existing SSH sessions. Closing this display stops polling, not transfers. Shortcuts: t overview · n next server · m compact GPUs · c choose servers · s shell · q close.

Mosh — Mobile Shell
Mosh starts mosh-server over SSH and keeps the terminal session responsive across IP changes, Wi-Fi roaming and temporary disconnects over encrypted UDP (ports 60000–61000 by default).
Installer script — review before installing
Runs on the server through SSH with sudo when needed. Review the script before running it; only configured system repositories are used.

Unknown host key
Compare this fingerprint with the one the server's own console shows, or with the one your server administrator published. Connecting without checking it lets anybody who can redirect your connection read and change your files.
Custom commands

Saved command templates. Write {file} where the selected name belongs; it is quoted the way the LinSCP command line reads quotes, never handed to a shell. A remote command runs in the session the panel is connected to, a local one through the same engine. Every run asks first and shows the command it will use.

        LinSCP Commander
        
      

      

        
Sessions opens the site manager: stored sessions are shared with the
        console client, and each tab keeps its own connection open.

        
Transfers run in the queue at the bottom. They can be paused,
        cancelled and retried; a cancelled transfer does not disturb the session.
        You can also drop individual files from your desktop onto the remote pane to upload them.

        
Synchronize compares the two panes and shows the plan before it
        changes anything. "Both" uses the record of the previous synchronization to
        tell a change from a conflict.

        
View (F3) opens a selected text file read-only. Edit (F4)
        opens a local or remote text file in the built-in editor. Saving checks that
        the file has not changed since it was opened; remote edits upload to the server.

        
Commander keys: F1 help, F2 rename, F3 view, F4 edit, F5 copy to the
        other panel, F6 move files to the other panel, F7 new directory, F8 delete,
        F9 properties/rights, F10 close session. Ctrl+A selects all; Enter opens a
        directory; Backspace goes up one level. Move is available for files; folders
        can still be copied, but are not moved by the cross-panel move action.

        
The LinSCP command console runs commands in the live session of the current tab.
